The architectural blueprint fundamentally restructures sports analytics by aggressively decoupling the spatial tracking pipeline from the uncertainty engine. The core mathematical thesis relies on establishing 'mathematically absolute' data geometry before permitting any deep learning or execution. This is achieved through hard physical constraints, such as vetoing spatial coordinates yielding velocities >13 m/s, which immediately filters out ~19% of corrupted telemetry. Simultaneously, the market microstructure is purified using a quadratic Shin devigging operator, which models the overround as an asymmetric defense against insider trading, thereby extracting true fair probabilities without the bias of proportional normalization. 

To guarantee predictive reliability under Knightian uncertainty, the system employs Conformalized Quantile Regression (CQR). A critical failure mode identified is 'fake-tightness,' where naive implementations clamp the conformal rank index k when the calibration set size n is too small (specifically, when n < \lceil 1/\alpha \rceil - 1). The blueprint mandates a fail-closed gate here: no clamping is allowed, resulting in infinite prediction intervals when finite-sample guarantees cannot be met. Furthermore, temporal dynamics like 'steam' are modeled using parameter-free B-spline geometric paths rather than Hawkes processes, avoiding overfitting to high-frequency noise on short horizons. Finally, by keeping the performance model (team strength) strictly decoupled from the market model (odds), the architecture prevents target leakage, ensuring that closing lines do not parrot the oddsmaker's biases back into the strength estimator.
